data.text:
Manila is wetter than I have seen it in a very long time, notwithstanding that it is monsoon season and that this is compounded by low pressure systems and typhoon activity, which is normal at this time of year.  

Many people are currently stranded, and many others are battling flood waters affecting their homes, business, and work.  Losses and damage will run into 100s of millions for sure! 

Friends are sharing photos and videos of Filipino resilience in the face of floodwater adversity.  Some are quite funny.  I don't know whether to laugh or cry at these.  Why should Filipinos and residents here just put up with things?  Why can't things be managed better?   

I do believe that flood control in Philippines is an uphill battle with contributing factors including the construction of businesses and residences in known flood zones. People do indeed have to live somewhere.  Many of the worst flood zones are low-income areas with all the problems of poor construction and poor planning (or no planning).  Flooding in one area, will cause back up of water in other areas and the problems just escalate.

Flooding is also made far worse by the perenial garbage situation which clogs everything, problems with completion of flood management projects, deforestation and forest management (forest can hold water and release it slowly), undersized and poorly maintained drainage (huge challenge), blocking of natural waterways, etc. 

There are no easy solutions even if the huge amounts of money spent on flood remediation in recent years all went to where it was supposed to go, which it surely didn't.  

The weather in the next few years is expected to be wetter than usual due not to man-made climate change but due to the eruption of the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha’apai volcano on Jan. 15, 2022. This was an underwater eruption that forced massive amounts of water into the atmosphere, estimated to be equivalent to about a 10% addition to typical atmospheric water levels.  There will other underwater volcanoes contributing as well. 

What goes up, must eventually come down and the planners and developers need to take water flows and worst-case scenario water volumes into account. 

Please avoid wading in contaminated flood waters if you possibly can; leptospirosis is but one of the known risks, and it can be deadly.  Local governments and health centers provide prophylactic antibiotics (single dose doxycycline) for exposed persons.

For anyone concerned, I am fine and only dealing with damp and minor residential leaking.  I am fortunate to live in an area that does not suffer from critical flooding.    Many of my friends and colleagues are not so fortunate.
